text:
alex: Quick q — running into weird behavior when cancelling streaming responses from the Node SDK. AbortController aborts the fetch but the server keeps generating and the SDK later emits duplicate partial tokens because retry logic kicks in. Anyone seen this?

maria: I hit this last week in a demo. Which SDK version? We tweaked retry defaults recently and streaming cancels might not be in the matrix. :thinking_face: 

alex: Node v1.2.3. Minimal repro: 
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
const stream = await client.responses.stream({ input: 'long gen' }, { signal: ac.signal });
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 500);
// SDK still emits a few chunks and then 'aborted' later, sometimes retries and replay partials
```

sam: FYI aborting a fetch only closes the local reader. The server / runtime may keep producing until it notices the socket close. Some infra (HTTP/1.1 long polling) is flaky. In our infra we added an explicit cancel path/header to actively stop generation, but not every SDK uses it.

jordan: In Go we use context.Context and cancel; with gRPC cancel that propagates nicely. HTTP streaming is messier — for dedicated infra we wire an `x-client-cancel: <req-id>` header that triggers server-side cancellation. That header isn't standard in SDKs yet.

maria: Proposed cross-SDK behavior:
1) abort should send an explicit cancel signal to server (when supported) e.g., `x-infer-abort: <req-id>`
2) close/cleanup local stream immediately
3) mark the request as non-retriable (so retries never replay partial streams)
4) emit a clear "aborted" event/state to the user
This should avoid duplicate partials and make semantics consistent across Node/Python/Go.

li: For Python the idioms are different — users expect `asyncio.wait_for` or httpx cancel tokens. Suggest we expose a `cancel_token()` helper on client that maps to `AbortController` for JS, `Context` for Go, and an async cancel token for Python. Docs + examples required.

alex: Also a streaming edge: if we buffer partial tokens locally (for buffering+resume) we must not mark those requests retryable. Partial buffering + retry = duplicated tokens. We should avoid automatic retry on any streamed request that emitted bytes.

sam: I'll draft a minimal Node PR: add `x-infer-abort` header on AC abort, set request.retryable = false, and ensure stream closes immediately. Will add unit tests mocking the server that assert header present and no retry.

maria: I'll prepare the Python pattern + docs update. Example snippet I plan to add: 
```py
# with httpx async client
async with client.stream("POST", "/v1/responses") as r:
    token = client.cancel_token()
    # cancel after timeout
    await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
    token.cancel()
    # r.aiter_text() should stop and raise CancelledError
```

jordan: I'll check Go side for headers + make sure context cancel maps to sending a cancel request when using HTTP streaming (we may need to call a /cancel endpoint in some infra modes).

devops-bot: deploy/devex-sdks v1.2.4 to staging complete :rocket:

alex: Thanks everyone. @sam @maria @jordan can we sync 10am PT tomorrow (15m) to align tests + docs? :thumbsup:

jordan: yup, added to calendar.

li: I'll add the test matrix to the issue: node/python/go × hosted/dedicated + streaming/cancel/retry cases.

alex: perfect — goal: consistent abort semantics (explicit cancel header when available, immediate local stop, no retries) and short docs snippets for each language.
